title: Late-watch brief and followups
content:
Late watch notes (shift: 03/18 23:00 - 03/19 07:00)

Quick summary:
- Two noisy pages overnight: one transient backend error spike (INF-2417) and one model-serving degraded tail latency alert.
- Both resolved with fallback routing + temporary scale-up, but follow-ups required to avoid recurrence.
- No customer-facing incidents opened; internal ticket created for post-mortem/root-cause.

Timeline (approx):
- 23:14 Pager: backend-err spike (rate of 5xxs jumped from ~0.01% -> 2%)
  - Initial action: rolled failed hostset (asg) via infra play (tools/infra/replace-hostset) — reduced 5xx to ~0.1% by 23:26
  - Note: root cause looks like a bad kernel upgrade on a small percentage of nodes (taints matched). Need to confirm with infra team.
- 01:02 Alert: model-serving tail-latency > SLO (p95-> p99 increase; error budget burn ~0.8%)
  - Mitigation: enabled canary fallback policy to smaller-medium model variant (model-v2-small) for affected tenant pool at 01:10; latency recovered by 01:18
  - Observed increased token-cost for some requests due to fallback; tracked in temporary billing log.

Immediate followups/notes to self:
- INF-2417: add post-mortem stub, assign to Jordan for infra confirmation (kernel upgrade timeline).
- Follow up with infra on taint rules: why nodes with partial upgrade remained in routing pool? (Slack convo: #infra-upgrades, ref thread ts:2026-03-18_23:45)
- Add additional healthcheck gating in autoscaler so hosts with pending reboots are evicted earlier (PR candidate: GH PR 2134 referenced).
- Model-serving: run a short A/B to verify fallback model quality not regressing for a amp-sensitive tenant (reach out to product owner Priya).

Runbook TODOs (priority ordered):
1) backend-5xx-runbook — clarify kernel/upgrade checks + commands to safely quarantine nodes.
   - Add exact kubectl / aws cli commands I used: 
     - aws autoscaling detach-instances --instance-ids <id> --auto-scaling-group-name <asg>
     - kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
   - Add observability run: query for kernel package versions across nodes (ansible facts or CMDB query).
2) tail-latency-fallback — document when to flip fallback policy vs scale up; include cost/budget checklist.
   - Add small script to estimate cost delta when fallback is on (quick heuristic: fallback_token_multiplier = 1.12).
3) paging-noise-filter — revisit alert thresholds for backend-5xx spike detector to reduce false positives; add cooldown window.

Notes/Diagnostics collected (for ticket):
- Kibana query snippets used:
  - 5xx count: service:backend AND status:[500 TO 599] AND timestamp:[now-15m TO now]
  - tail latency: metric(serving.latency.p99{model=serving-model,tenant=~".*-tenant"})
- Logs: attached samples in INF-2417 (errors show malformed http2 frames + kernel msg: 'XDP: drop due to busy queue')
- Grafana dashboard snapshots saved to /dashboards/snapshots/INF-2417-2026-03-19.png

Handover bullets for morning shift (6:45am):
- Check INF-2417 for infra reply; if infra confirms kernel rollout, schedule node drains for remainder of cluster after windows agreed.
- Verify fallback policy revert timeline: if degradation not observed in 4 hours, revert to primary model route and run automated quality checks (eval set).
- Validate cost impact: billing-team tag should be updated in ticket if estimated delta > $150/day.
- Follow up with product owner Priya on small A/B for fallback quality (ticket: INF-2417-AB).

Open questions / things to research quickly:
- Is there a way to have autoscaler avoid recently-upgraded nodes for X minutes? Check ASG lifecycle hooks.
- Can we add token-level cost tracing to fallback path so we can emit accurate billing deltas in real time?

Commands I ran (copyable):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep reboot
- kubectl describe node <suspect-node> | egrep -i 'kernel|kmod|taint'
- aws autoscaling terminate-instance-in-auto-scaling-group --instance-id i-0abc123 --should-decrement-desired-capacity false

Loose ideas for long-term changes:
- Add model-variant canaries at proxy layer (route 5% of traffic to fallback to watch for quality/cost) with automatic rollback if eval fails.
- Better tagging of hosts with "upgrade_stage" metadata so routing decisions can avoid them until healthy.

Stuff to put on my personal checklist (day after):
- Draft runbook updates and open PRs for review (assign infra owners).
- Sync with Priya for AB test parameters.
- Run through simulated incident drill for upgrade-related 5xx (create synthetic traffic test).

Random notes to self:
- Coffee next shift.
- Remember to push GH PR template that includes precise commands and safety checks.

End of notes.
